LESSON: WEAVING CRAFT

Grade: PP1
Subject: PSYCHOMOTOR AND CREATIVE ACTIVITIES
Strand: PAPER
Topic 5.1: Weaving CRAFT

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Weaving CRAFT. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: What do you use the b) Weave using papers for fun. of paper strips woven materials for?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. Appreciate own and others work • Learners work in pairs, small groups as they practice weaving. • Learners observe safety as they work in groups. • Learners display their work and gallery walk

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: WEAVING CRAFT
Subject: PSYCHOMOTOR AND CREATIVE ACTIVITIES · Grade: PP1
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Weaving CRAFT helps you succeed in PSYCHOMOTOR AND CREATIVE ACTIVITIES. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

KEY FACTS: WEAVING CRAFT
Study Weaving CRAFT like a learner textbook page: meaning → examples → practice → check.
Replace teacher words with your own words.
If a step is unclear, rewrite it shorter and try again.

PART 1: Appreciate own and others work • Learners work in pairs, small groups as they practice weaving. • Learners observe safety as they work in groups. • Learners display their work and gallery walk

What this means
In this part you learn to Appreciate own and others work • Learners work in pairs, small groups as they practice weaving. • Learners observe safety as they work in groups. • Learners display their work and gallery walk. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: Appreciate own and others work • Learners work in pairs, small groups as they practice weaving. • Learners observe safety as they work in groups. • Learners display their work and gallery walk.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Value in action: Show how “Weaving CRAFT” looks when you treat a classmate kindly.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can Appreciate own and others work • Learners work in pairs, small groups as they practice weaving. • Learners observe safety as they work in groups. • Learners display their work and gallery walk. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Weaving CRAFT is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Show how “Weaving CRAFT” looks when you treat a classmate kindly. (skill: Appreciate own and others work • Learners work in pairs, small groups as they practice weaving. • Learners observe safety as they work in groups. • Learners display their work and gallery walk)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Weaving CRAFT to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: Appreciate own and others work • Learners work in pairs, small groups as they practice weaving. • Learners observe safety as they work in groups. • Learners display their work and gallery walk.
3. Make one local Kenya example of Weaving CRAFT from your county, market, farm, or school.
4. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Weaving CRAFT: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a PP1 learner study Weaving CRAFT?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. What do you use the b) Weave using papers for fun. of paper strips woven materials for?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Weaving CRAFT means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: Appreciate own and others work • Learners work in pairs, small groups as they practice weaving. • Learners observe safety as they work in groups. • Learners display their work and gallery walk.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
